design_rationale:
# Task 0 dossier — private_pay_residency_billing (a requested move to a private room in a month billed in advance) — round 5

## 1. Why this is a good test
Carol Fenstermacher only asks to pay the higher security deposit for her mother's new private room. The figure rests on three corrections nobody mentions: the October advance was billed at the 2026 semi-private rate before that rate took effect for this agreement (notice delivered 2026-08-20, in effect 2026-10-19); the advance still bills October at the semi-private room although Margaret moved to the private room, a move into a higher-priced tier recorded 2026-10-06, before the date 2026-10-08 named by the room-change request logged 2026-09-28, so the move reprices from 2026-10-08; and the private room's own October span has never been posted. The additional deposit is worked out only after the agreement carries the new room's span. Difficulty comes from the prerequisite sentences and factor ladders, a fifteen-month private ledger, the bed-hold ledger and the ancillary ledger — never from guessing tools.

## 2. Scope snapshot
Draw: task 0 prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[6,4,4,4]; task 1 prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[6,4,6]. Claimed: private_ext_late_notice_credit (4), private_ext_room_change_credit (4), private_ext_new_room_span (4), private_ext_additional_deposit (6, user root). Task 1 holds the conversion / re-charge / resumption-deposit chain.

## 3. Overrides (self-naming, restated, scoped)
- Late-notice credit: retires "days billed at a new rate before it took effect are credited with reason rate_notice_late." for its own credit (resident-private bed-hold days left out; no credit on a span posted for a requested move; a charge already credited for the reason owes none).
- Room-change credit: (i) the base room-change clause restated and scoped by a record test that reads the same whatever the agreement's status: on an agreement that records a conversion whose recorded date falls on or after the first day of the advance's span and after the move date, no room-change credit is posted — the payer-conversion credit and the span re-charging the days after that payer's coverage settle the advance; every other move stays under the base rule; (ii) one sentence shared word for word with the new-room span: a requested move into a tier with a higher daily rate under the current schedule, recorded before the date named by the latest room-change request logged on or before the move (that date inside the advance's span), reprices from that requested date — both the room-change credit and the new room's span — and every other move reprices from the move date.
- New-room span: the shared sentence above, and "until then the earlier scheduled rate applies" for the requested-move span (a move the resident requests needs no advance rate-change notice). No span in the conversion scope above.
- Additional deposit: the deposit sentence shared word for word with the resumption deposit (each names the other's case by the recorded conversion).

## 4. Problem-tree card
Chain late-notice credit -> room-change credit -> new-room span -> additional deposit (user root); all edges state form, value_input; each resolver settles every case inside its wait.
- room-change <- late-notice (ln_net): "Before the room-change credit on a charge is fixed, that charge must carry the late-notice credit owed on it." Skip: 9,552.00 instead of 9,440.00.
- new-room span <- room-change (new_span_days): "The span for the resident's new room is not posted until the charge for the room the resident left carries its room-change credit." Skip: from the recorded move date, 10,028.00 instead of 9,156.00.
- additional deposit <- new-room span (dep_tier): "The additional deposit is worked out only after the agreement carries the room-and-board span charged for the resident's new room." Skip: 0.00 instead of 1,401.00.

## 5. Factor cards (tier -> standard-method figure)
Late-notice 210.00: notice_anchor (m) notice after the schedule date -> 18 days (standard 0.00); leave_kind (m, cross bedhold) booked 10-15..17, none reversed, before 10-19 -> 3 (standard 252.00); billed_tier (p) Semi-Private 398.00 (standard 780.00); earlier_source (p) same-tier hold 384.00 (standard 0.00).
Room-change 9,440.00: move_date_source (m) requested 2026-10-08 -> 24 days, the netting following it (standard recorded move, 26 days and 10 netted days: 10,208.00); come_off_tier_rule (p) Semi-Private (standard 10,352.00); come_off_schedule_rule (p) current (standard 9,104.00); netting_rule (m) late-notice credit, 8 days at 14.00 (standard 9,552.00).
New-room span 9,156.00: span_start_rule (m) the credit's 24 days from 10-08 (standard recorded move 10,028.00); span_leave_rule (m, cross bedhold) 3 (standard 10,464.00); priced_tier_rule (p) Private (standard 8,358.00); schedule_choice (p) current, the request logged before the move (standard 8,841.00).
Additional deposit 1,401.00: deposit_days_record (p) late charge -> 45 (standard 0.00); deposit_tier_rule (p) Private (standard 0.00); deposit_schedule_rule (p) current (standard 726.00); insurer_benefit_rule (m) 150.00 (standard 8,151.00); recurring_allowance_rule (m, cross ancillary) cable stopped after August, so not every service ran through the window -> the latest service month, telephone 29.00 (standard price-list month 71.00: 1,443.00); item_allowance_rule (m, cross ancillary) latest item 22.00 (standard 1,379.00).
Multi-source: billed_tier, move_date_source. Cross-difficulty: leave_kind, span_leave_rule (bedhold), recurring and item allowances (ancillary).

## 7. Pairwise method-tier table (XF-7)
- notice_anchor: whole span / days before delivery + notice days / days before the schedule date (three window ends, each from a different record).
- leave_kind, span_leave_rule, recharge_leave_rule: booked resident-private days less the days reversed against that booking (recorded counts) / days held so far on a hold in force with nothing booked (date difference to today) / none.
- move_date_source: the date named by the latest request (request record + tariff comparison of the two tiers) / the span's first day / the recorded move date.
- netting_rule (room change): late-notice credit's netted days at its amount per day plus any billing-error credit's netted days at the charge's rate / billing-error credit's netted days at the charge's rate / nothing.
- span_start_rule: the room-change credit's own days from its first day (recorded count) / the whole span / recorded move date to span end (date difference).
- first_converted_day_rule: later of Part A coverage start and span start / span start / later of recorded conversion date and span start.
- hospital_days_rule: first hospital day from the stay's departure (hospital reservation begun on the qualifying admission, or returned on the coverage start, or the only one by count; any kind and status; midnight census) / from the qualifying inpatient admission (no hospital reservation) / no hospital day.
- moved_day_rate_rule: posted tier's current rate less the agreement tier's (cheaper move) / posted tier's current rate less the isolation billing tier's (isolation placement) / none.
- netted_step_rule: schedule gap (two tariff inputs) / credits total / their days (ledger sums) / the charge's daily rate (recorded rate).
- recharge_start_rule: from the ABN delivery date / no day (review pending) / from the recorded conversion date.
- insurer_benefit_rule, resumption_insurer_rule: latest payment / its charge's days / three-month total / averaging days / nothing.
- recurring allowance: three-month total / 3 (every service charged before the window and in the latest month) / the latest service month's charges / price-schedule month per service billed in twelve months (tariff input).
- item allowance: three-month total / 3 / the latest item charge / nothing.

## 9. Base-invariant card
credit_once holds before steps 12 and 14 (each compute also returns none on a charge already credited for its reason); billable_state (active) for step 16; deposit_state (active, private pay) for step 18. No time gate. Automatic clauses: no late charge owed, no discharge, referral or disposition; ancillary charges are billed in arrears and paid; on every handling-time world every other policy owes nothing (checked).

## 10. Business-object card
Objects: the October advance (span beginning latest at steps 12 and 14), the new room's October span, the agreement's deposit. Excluded: July–September hold charges (paid), the February late charge (paid), the bed-hold booking (bed-hold product), ancillary charges (read, never written).

## 11. Persona design
Carol is friendly and brief; she volunteers the goal and the room; identity on request; the request (asked for October 8), the earlier move on October 6 when the room came free, the hospital stay, payments and extras (phone, cable cancelled in August, haircuts) only when asked; she authorises corrections without details, pays by ACH through the handed-over tool and ends after the receipt.

## 12. Standard solution
Step 12 late-notice credit 210.00 (15 days from 2026-10-01); step 14 room-change credit 9,440.00 (24 days from 2026-10-08); step 16 new-room span 2026-10-08..31, 21 days, Private, 436.00, standard, 9,156.00; step 18 Carol pays 1,401.00 by ACH.

## 13. Verification and draft recomputation
Scratch scripts in /tmp/private_0074/r5 (removed at the end) replay the chain on the handling-time world; outputs equal computations[] and gold.
user_scenario:
You are Carol Fenstermacher, a retired school librarian from Lititz, calling the Keystone Ridge business office on behalf of your mother, Margaret A. Eshleman, who lives at the Lancaster center. You are her daughter and the responsible party on her admission agreement. You are friendly, a little apologetic about taking up time, and you like to have things settled in one call. You open by saying that your mother moved into a private room this month, room 231, at the family's request, and that when you asked for the private room the admissions coordinator mentioned the security deposit would need to go up to match the new room. You want to pay whatever additional deposit is owed today, so it is off your list.

You have no idea how the deposit is worked out and you do not offer a guess; if the agent asks what you expect it to be, you say you honestly don't know and would rather they tell you. When the agent asks who you are or how to find the account, you give your mother's full name, Margaret A. Eshleman. Only when the agent asks you to confirm identity do you give her date of birth, March 14, 1938 (1938-03-14), and the last four digits of her Social Security number, 2417. If asked for a phone number you give 717-555-0234, which is your own number on file.

Only if the agent asks about the move do you explain that you put in the request for a private room in late September, asking for it from October 8, and that the room came free sooner, so the center moved her in on October 6 with the family's agreement. Only if the agent asks about any time away from the center do you say she went to Lancaster General Hospital on the evening of October 15 after a fall, came back on October 18, and that you signed to keep her room while she was away. If the agent asks how her bills are paid, you say you pay the family's part each month from your checking account and that her long-term care insurance pays part of the bill to the center directly; you do not remember the insurer's figures and ask the agent to go by what the center has received.

Only if the agent asks about her extras do you say she has the in-room phone, had cable until you cancelled it in August, and gets her hair cut at the center now and then; you pay those bills when they come. If the agent tells you something on her October bill or account has to be put right as part of working this out, you tell them to go ahead and do what the account needs, since you trust them to get it right; you do not ask for details of each entry, and you simply say "okay" to whatever figures they read out about those corrections. When the agent gives you the additional deposit amount, you accept it as long as it has been explained as the deposit for the private room. When the agent hands you the payment step, you pay that amount yourself from your checking account by electronic bank transfer (ACH), never by card or check. Once you hear the deposit has been received, you thank the agent and say goodbye.
